artists.biography:
Mr. Big is an American rock supergroup, formed in Los Angeles, California in 1988. The band is a quartet composed of Eric Martin (lead vocals), Paul Gilbert (guitar), Billy Sheehan (bass guitar), and Pat Torpey (drums); The band is noted especially for their musicianship, and scored a number of hits. Their songs were often marked by strong vocals and vocal harmonies. Their hits include "To Be with You" (a number one single in 15 countries in 1991) and "Green-Tinted Sixties Mind".
Mr. Big have remained active and popular for over two decades, despite internal conflicts and changing music trends. They broke up in 2002, but after requests from fans, they reunited in 2009; their first tour was in Japan, in June 2009. The band released What If..., their first album in 10 years, in January 2011.
The band takes its name from the song by Free, which was eventually covered by the band on their 1993 album, Bump Ahead.

perplexity.description:
Lean into It is the second studio album by American rock band Mr. Big, originally released in 1991 on Atlantic Records. The album blends hard rock and pop sensibilities, showcasing the band's technical prowess and melodic songwriting. Known for its polished production and dynamic performances, the record features standout tracks such as the acoustic ballad "To Be with You," which became a global hit and reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100, and the energetic "Just Take My Heart," which also charted in the Top 20. The album's musical style balances guitar-driven rock with accessible hooks, reflecting the band's reputation as a hard rock supergroup.

Lean into It marked a turning point in Mr. Big's career, establishing them as major players in the early 1990s rock scene. It was their commercial breakthrough, peaking at number 15 on the Billboard 200 and earning widespread recognition for its blend of virtuosic musicianship and radio-friendly songcraft. The album has since been recognized as a notable entry in the hair metal genre, ranking on lists such as Rolling Stone's 50 Greatest Hair Metal Albums of All Time. Its success solidified Mr. Big's place in rock history and remains their most celebrated release.
